title: Finite free change of rings exchanges quotient completion on arbitrary complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $R\to S$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ as an $R$-module sheaf for some finite $d\geq0$. Let $t\in R(1)$ and $v\in S(1)$ be global sections with injective multiplication on their respective rings, and suppose the image of $t$ is $uv^e$ for a unit $u\in S(1)^\times$ and an integer $e\geq1$. Assume countable products of $R$-modules, $S$-modules and abelian sheaves are exact. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived change of rings $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the strict quotient completions
$$C_RQ=R\lim_{n\geq1}(Q\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/t^nR),\qquad C_SH=R\lim_{m\geq1}(H\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S/v^mS).$$
Here quotients are sheaf quotients, tensors are K-flat total tensors [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the derived limits and units $\eta^R,\eta^S$ are the strict-tower derived limits [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] with the quotient augmentations, represented by a product map and zero shifted-product component. For every $Q\in D(R)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\epsilon_Q:T C_RQ\xrightarrow{\sim}C_STQ,\qquad \epsilon_Q\,T(\eta^R_Q)=\eta^S_{TQ}.$$
It is specified by the canonical tensor/product map on the $t$-tower, the identifications $(R/t^nR)\otimes_R S=S/v^{en}S$, and the inverse of the specified arithmetic-subsequence Roos comparison of [lem-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction]. It is independent of the basis of $S$. No completeness or boundedness hypothesis on $Q$ is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain CR and CS separately from existence of principal quotient completion. Obtain the balanced strict-tower comparisons, canonical product and cone maps δ and arithmetic maps a from finiteFreeQuotientRoosComparison. These data are natural on all cochain maps; ordinary finite-free extension is exact, so its derived counit is invertible on every complex. The standard Mathlib universal-property lemma for an already-inverting functor gives invertibility of the derived counit directly; no triangulated-functor comparison is needed. Preservation of every K-flat representative uses the independent-coefficient tensor-cancellation proof, separately from the finite free comparison.

On each K-flat P compose T(CR.counit_P), the change-of-rings counit at the source Roos complex, Q(δ_P), the inverse of Q(a_P), the inverse target completion counit, and the inverse target image of the change-of-rings counit. Naturality follows by cancellation of the target counit and arithmetic isomorphisms. The two-variable K-flat localization theorem implies one-variable descent by holding one variable fixed at a resolving object. Descend the representative natural isomorphism; a flat K-flat resolution recovers its formula on every K-flat P.

Product projections and the balanced quotient-map equation show E(quotientProduct_R) c = quotientProduct_S selection. Compare the two cone coordinates using the normalizations in CR and CS; the first coordinates are zero and the second are this product equation. This proves E(augmentation_R) δ = augmentation_S a. Combine the counit and unit equations with naturality to prove the exchange unit equation on every K-flat P. Resolve arbitrary representatives and use localization natural-transformation extensionality to obtain it on all derived objects. Finally package β,c,δ,a and their prescribed formulas in RepresentativeComparison.

Edge cases d=0, t a unit, e=1, Q=0, and Z_p ⊂ Z_p[√p] with Q=Q_p or ⊕Z_p all behave correctly. theorem finiteFreeCompletionExchange
    (F : SheafOfModules.DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel.{u, v, r, wR, wS} φ)
    (_hfree : ∃ d : ℕ, Nonempty
      ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).map φ)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)) ≅
        ∐ (fun _ : Fin d ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
          (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))))
    (t : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)).sections)
    (vS : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)).sections)
    (_ht : Mono (globalSectionMultiplication R t))
    (_hv : Mono (globalSectionMultiplication S vS))
    (uS : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)).sections)
    (_hu : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, IsUnit (@id (S.obj.obj U) (uS.val U)))
    (e : ℕ) (_he : 1 ≤ e)
    (_hrelation : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ,
      φ.hom.app U (@id (R.obj.obj U) (t.val U)) =
        (@id (S.obj.obj U) (uS.val U)) * (@id (S.obj.obj U) (vS.val U)) ^ e)
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ)
      (ringedSiteModules.{r} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ)
      (ringedSiteModules.{r} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{r})] :
    ∃ (CR : Model R t) (CS : Model S vS)
      (ε : CR.completion ⋙ F.T ≅ F.T ⋙ CS.completion),
      (∀ Q, F.T.map (CR.unit.app Q) ≫ ε.hom.app Q = CS.unit.app (F.T.obj Q)) ∧
      (∀ P, CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := R) P →
        Nonempty (RepresentativeComparison F t vS e CR CS ε P))
